seeded_faults.trigger: A source-owned public field changes for an existing stable identity.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The destination record is recreated or associated by mutable public fields.

seeded_faults.trigger: Two fallback identities contain delimiter-bearing fields with the same concatenated text.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Distinct source identities collide.

seeded_faults.trigger: Equivalent source and destination text uses composed/decomposed Unicode or outer whitespace.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Equivalent identities fragment.

seeded_faults.trigger: One payload repeats a stable identity with a later corrected row.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The destination contains duplicate identities or ignores deterministic last-row precedence.

seeded_faults.trigger: Two legacy destination records share fallback fields and receive two distinct stable identities.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: One destination instance is assigned to more than one stable identity.

seeded_faults.trigger: An excluded legacy row later receives a stable identity.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The excluded identity reappears.

seeded_faults.trigger: A live update changes source-owned fields for records with destination history.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Destination-owned identifiers and history are reset.

seeded_faults.trigger: A stable source identity is synchronized into an existing destination record.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The destination instance identity changes.

seeded_faults.trigger: A destination record has a completed or winning state before synchronization.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The destination status is reset while visible fields remain correct.

seeded_faults.trigger: A destination record has material history before synchronization.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: History arrays are emptied or reassigned.

seeded_faults.trigger: The destination maintains a secondary collection of completed records.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The primary record remains but its secondary-list membership is lost.

seeded_faults.trigger: A message arrives from an unconfigured origin with otherwise valid content.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The message enters the handoff path.

seeded_faults.trigger: A same-origin sibling window sends a valid-looking message.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: A message from the wrong window peer enters the handoff path.

seeded_faults.trigger: Replacement completion is received before READY and transfer.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The sender accepts out-of-phase completion.

seeded_faults.trigger: A duplicate or reordered synchronization sequence arrives.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Older state is accepted.

seeded_faults.trigger: Normalization yields no rows while the authoritative source still declares records.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: A malformed or transient payload clears valid destination state.

seeded_faults.trigger: The authoritative source intentionally reaches zero records.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Obsolete destination records remain.

seeded_faults.trigger: Persistence rejects an accepted sequence and the same sequence is retried.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The safe retry is classified as stale.

seeded_faults.trigger: The application emits success while persistence is still pending.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: Public completion precedes durable state.

seeded_faults.trigger: Persistence rejects after the in-memory state was prepared.
seeded_faults.expected_failure: The application reports success for an uncommitted state.
